# Meet the data

The main lesson reads `data/hypertension/`. The inputs have the same orientation used in synthetic practice.

| File | Rows | Sample columns / required metadata |
|---|---|---|
| `sample-metadata.tsv` | 140 samples | `sample_id`, `group`, subject and source identifiers |
| `taxon-abundance.tsv` | 440 species | 140 sample accessions; first header `taxon_id` |
| `functional-features.tsv` | 483 named pathways | 140 sample accessions; first header `feature_id` |

Metadata has **samples in rows**; abundance tables have **samples in columns**.

## Inspect the inputs

Copy this block into Bash/Zsh. For Windows alternatives, see [setup](../../00-setup.qmd#copy-code-into-the-right-place).

```bash
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
folder = Path("data/hypertension")
meta = pd.read_csv(folder / "sample-metadata.tsv", sep="\t")
taxa = pd.read_csv(folder / "taxon-abundance.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0)
functions = pd.read_csv(folder / "functional-features.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0)
print("Metadata rows:", len(meta))
print("Taxon table:", taxa.shape)
print("Functional table:", functions.shape)
print(meta.groupby("group").size())
print("Distinct subjects:", meta.subject_id.nunique())
print(meta.head(3).to_string(index=False))
PY
```

Expect **140**, **(440, 140)**, **(483, 140)**, **41 Control**, **99 HTN**, and **140 distinct subjects**.

## Metadata and units

`sample_id` is the ENA run accession matching abundance columns. `subject_id` identifies the participant; `source_sample_id` preserves the original identifier. `number_reads` records source read depth, not the sum of either abundance table.

Groups come from curated `study_condition`. The broader source `disease` field combines pre-hypertension and hypertension and cannot recover the three groups. These are source labels, not diagnostic rules for new patients. Age, sex and BMI are absent from the pinned metadata snapshot; no covariates were inferred from sample names.

Only species-level rows were retained. Mixing species with higher ranks would count the same taxonomic profiles repeatedly. Species values are percentages, approximately summing to 100.

Pathway values are HUMAnN relative abundances. Only unstratified named pathways were retained. Taxon-stratified contributions would double count pathway totals. `UNMAPPED` and `UNINTEGRATED` are excluded from the pathway table and recorded separately. The retained named pathways do not sum to one on the source scale.

| Supporting file | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `taxon-annotations.tsv` | Species IDs, labels and full source lineages |
| `functional-annotations.tsv` | MetaCyc IDs, labels and full source feature names |
| `functional-denominators.tsv` | Unmapped, unintegrated and named-pathway source totals |
| `measurement-info.json` | Units and interpretation restrictions |
| `../provenance/hypertension/` | Source matrices, pinned metadata, checksums and validation |

No abundance filtering was applied during export. In this subset, 31 species and five pathways are all zero. They do not affect Shannon or positive-total normalization; downstream statistical methods may require an explicit filtering rule.

## Optional full cohort

`data/hypertension-all-groups/` contains **196 unique subjects**, including **56 pHTN**. Both subsets use the same feature definitions. The complete cohort includes hypertension sample **ERR1398137**, source ID **H2M413924**. See provenance records for the reconciliation against earlier input versions.

Learners analyse the supplied TSVs with Python. Maintainers can reproduce their export with `scripts/R/prepare_hypertension.R`; R is not required for the learner workflow.

**Your task:** locate ERR1398068 in all three inputs and explain why a taxonomic total near 100 is not sequencing depth.
